We were unable to complete the planned revision of our system based on a fuller discourse analysis of the texts. We have since implemented many of these changes and can now report preliminary and encouraging results of basing our system on XML markup of texts with syntactic and semantic attributes and use of XML stylesheet functionality (specifically, XPath expressions) to answer questions. The official confidence-weighted score for the main TREC-11 QA task was 0.049, based on processing 20 of the top 50 documents provided by NIST. Our estimated mean reciprocal rank was 0.128 for the exact answers and 0.227 for sentence answers, comparable to our results from previous years. With our revised XML-based system, using a 20 percent sample of the TREC questions, we have an estimated confidence-weighted score of 0.869 and mean reciprocal rank of 0.828. We describe our system and examine the results from XML tagging in terms of question-answering and other applications such as information extraction, text summarization, novelty studies, and regulatory documents. In contrast to traditional means to access information in the domain, the proposed system attempts to deliver an accurate and precise answer to user queries. This is accomplished by a two-step approach which first selects relevant paragraphs given a question; and then compares the selected paragraph with user query to predict a span in the paragraph as the answer. We employ neural network based solutions for each step, and compare them with existing, and alternate baselines. We perform our evaluations with a gold-standard benchmark comprising over 600 questions on the MaRisk regulatory document. In our experiments, we observe that our proposed system outperforms other BV","content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"abstract":"<jats:p>In this paper, we focus on a novel task, to introduce a unified platform that deals with multiple research directions. An instance, the goal of temporal moment localization in videos using natural language is to locate the moment that corresponds to the input query, and output is moment\/answer of the query. Similar to this, the goal of video and image question answering is to use input questions to locate the correct answer within the video and image. For every task listed above, the input consists of video, image, and query\/question, while the output is visual from video or image. We present the first study on a unified framework for chronological modality refinement (CMR) that, offers a single platform to address temporal moment localization, video, and image question answering, elimination of modality entanglement, and successful implementation of modality collaboration. Our CMR include a temporal pyramid (TP) module with $ m $ blocks and a distinctive transformer architecture that takes both video and image as input. To further reinforce the unified design, we introduce a lightweight Unified Task Routing Module (UTRM) that automatically identifies active modality configurations and routes video, image, and language features to their appropriate processing paths, enabling seamless task-adaptive behavior within the unified architecture. This routing mechanism enhances feature consistency across tasks and ensures that temporal, spatial, and linguistic reasoning remain disentangled yet collaborative. Combined with our refinement modules, UTRM significantly improves the generalization ability of CMR across heterogeneous multimodal tasks. We employ various datasets Charades-STA, TACoS, Activity-Net, TGIF-QA, MSVD, and MSRVTT-QA related to above mentioned research directions, and results demonstrate the effectiveness of our CMR approach.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.2139\/ssrn.6516277","type":"posted-content","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,4,3]],"date-time":"2026-04-03T19:42:11Z","timestamp":1775245331000},"source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Temporal commonly-used large-scale knowledge bases have been facing challenges in open domain question answering tasks which are caused by the loose knowledge association and weak structural logic of triplet-based knowledge. To find a way out of this dilemma, this work proposes a novel metaknowledge enhanced approach for open domain question answering. We design an automatic approach to extract metaknowledge and build metaknowledge network from Wiki documents. For the purpose of representing the directional weighted graph with hierarchical and semantic features, we present an original graph encoder GE4MK to model the metaknowledge network. Then a metaknowledge enhanced graph reasoning model MEGr-Net is proposed for question answering, which aggregates both relational and neighboring interactions comparing with R-GCN and GAT. Experiments have proved the improvement of metaknowledge over main-stream triplet-based knowledge. We have found that the graph reasoning models and pre-trained language models also have influences on the metaknowledge enhanced question answering
